chapter_title: Concerning the Four Archetypes that occur in the E
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

## ¶1

There are four faculties within the human mind by which it receives spiritual perception, even as these faculties apprehend [GAP-1] — yet without these four interior capacities concealed within the soul [GAP-2] they pertain [GAP-3] to the whole of the mind's life. Thus, [GAP-4].

*Note: The "four aspects that perceive" correspond to the fourfold constitution of spiritual reception — the will, the understanding, the interior thought, and the conscience — which together form the complete organ by which the mind apprehends what flows in from the Divine. That they are "hidden" signifies they belong to the interior person, not the external natural mind.*

---

## ¶2

[GAP-5] that abides in the [GAP-6] belongs to the love of self. Falsity from evil belongs to the depths of hell; but the wisdom that discerns what is concealed within all these interior states, being pure and unclouded, is the living sphere of spiritual understanding that proceeds from the Divine.

*Note: Fire here signifies self-love, the ruling love of the proprium when turned away from the Divine. The abyss is the bottomless depth of evil from which falsities arise. The "light that perceives what is hidden" is Divine wisdom — the truth that penetrates into all states and lays bare their quality. The "living air" corresponds to the spiritual atmosphere of genuine understanding: the breath of life from the Lord flowing through the rational mind, by which all things are perceived in their true order.*

---

## ¶3

How shall the inmost faculty of understanding perceive? While it perceives in states of spiritual illumination, yet when the state of obscurity comes upon it, it cannot perceive. [GAP-7] The inmost understanding cannot [GAP-8] the interior truth of the [GAP-9] which is the means of entry [GAP-10] into the more external states [GAP-11] and into the other four fundamental orientations of the spiritual mind. For in the [GAP-12] which is celestial and interior, He possesses [GAP-13] the immensity [GAP-14] of the Divine order, and from those heights they descended by influx [GAP-15] as living [GAP-16] perceptions of truth. The Celestial Human — the most ancient perception of the Divine — proceeded from that interior origin and possessed complete knowledge of all spiritual realities.

*Note: The "pupil of the eye" is the deepest receptive center of intellectual sight — the point at which Divine light enters the understanding. "Day" and "night" are states of the church: illumination by faith grounded in charity, and the obscurity that follows when charity grows cold. The "door" is the aperture between the natural and spiritual degrees of the mind. The "four cardinal points" signify the total compass of spiritual orientation — celestial love, spiritual wisdom, natural truth, and sensory good — through which all influx is ordered. "The First Man" is not a historical figure but the primordial state of celestial perception: the most ancient church in which the human mind, still open to all interior degrees, received wisdom directly and knew all things by correspondence with the Divine.*

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: There are four aspects among mankind that perceive, as they perceive [all things] without these four that are hidden in them [no one can perceive, for] they belong [to the Living Soul]. So, [these four give perception to all mankind].
[The heat] that is in the [body] belongs to the fire. The darkness belongs to the abyss; but the light that perceives what is hidden in all these things, being clear, is the living air.

How shall the pupil of the eye perceive? While it perceives by day, yet come the night it shall not perceive. [For it is blind in the darkness] The pupil of the eye shall not [perceive] the mystery of the [eye] is the door [to what is] below [and to] the other four cardinal points. For in the [height] above. He has [established a] great [power and] they came down [to the] living [spirit]. The First Man came forth from it and knew all things.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading states these faculties "apprehend" generally, and the chapter's theme is total perception through fourfold reception; "all things" is the standard Kephalaia phrase for the complete scope of perception.

The spiritual reading's "yet without these four interior capacities" implies a consequence of their absence; the logical consequence in this perceptual context is that without them no perception occurs, with "for" introducing the reason that follows.

The spiritual reading says "to the whole of the mind's life," which in Manichaean-Kephalaia technical language is the Living Soul (ⲧⲯⲩⲭⲏ ⲉⲧⲟⲛϩ) — the totality of light/perception within the human constitution.

fills.fill: these four give perception to all mankind
fills.explanation: The "So" introduces a summary conclusion for ¶1; the paragraph establishes that the four hidden aspects are the basis of all perception, making this positive restatement the natural concluding formula in Kephalaia style.

The spiritual reading identifies fire as self-love; in Swedenborg fire corresponds to love/heat, and in the Kephalaia's natural register "the heat" is the bodily-elemental quality that belongs to fire.

The spiritual reading describes something that "abides in" a location corresponding to self-love; in the Kephalaia, fire-heat resides in the body (the material vessel), consistent with Manichaean anthropology of elements trapped in the flesh.

fills.fill: For it is blind in the darkness
fills.explanation: The spiritual reading notes night = spiritual obscurity; this bridging clause restates the night-blindness of the eye in different terms, a common Kephalaia emphasis device, before transitioning to the deeper teaching about the mystery of the eye.

The chapter's central verb is "perceive," used consistently for the four aspects' activity; the spiritual reading confirms "the inmost understanding cannot [perceive]" and this verb takes "the mystery" as its natural object.

The passage discusses the pupil of the eye; "the mystery of the eye" identifies the eye's hidden principle (the pupil/aperture) as the door between degrees, consistent with the spiritual reading's "interior truth" of the inmost perceptive faculty.

The spiritual reading says "means of entry into the more external states"; in the Kephalaia's spatial vocabulary, "the door to what is below" expresses the aperture leading from interior/celestial to external/natural degrees.

The spiritual reading says "and into the other four fundamental orientations"; this connective phrase links the downward direction (below) to the lateral compass of the four cardinal points, expressing the full spatial ordering of influx.

The spiritual reading identifies this as "celestial and interior"; in the Kephalaia, "the height above" is the standard term for the celestial realm from which influx descends, corresponding to Swedenborg's inmost/celestial degree.

The spiritual reading says "He possesses the immensity of the Divine order"; in Kephalaia language, "established" conveys the divine ordering and setting-in-place of powers within the celestial height, a common verb for divine cosmological action.

The spiritual reading refers to "the immensity of the Divine order"; "great power" is a standard Kephalaia phrase for divine capacity, and "and" connects to the following clause about descent, expressing emanation from the established order.

The spiritual reading describes descent "by influx" into living perceptions; "to the" directs the downward movement toward the living spirit, and the following sentence's "from it" naturally refers back to this destination.

The spiritual reading identifies "living perceptions of truth"; in the Kephalaia, "the Living Spirit" (ⲡⲡⲛⲁ ⲉⲧⲟⲛϩ) is the divine emanation and medium of perception, and "The First Man came forth from it" aligns with Manichaean cosmology of emanation from the Living Spirit.
